title: verify_api_key bypasses FastAPI session lifetime management

evidence.quote:
session = next(get_session())

    # Check if any users exist
    has_users = session.exec(select(User)).first() is not None

def get_session() -> Generator[Session, None, None]:
    """
    Get a database session.

    Yields:
        SQLModel Session instance.
    """
    with Session(engine) as session:
        yield session

reasoning: verify_api_key manually calls next(get_session()) instead of declaring the session as a dependency or using an explicit context manager. The generator that owns the with Session(engine) block is not retained, so its cleanup is disconnected from the later queries and commits performed through the returned Session object. This makes transaction/connection lifetime fragile and can leave reopened session resources dependent on garbage collection under request load.
recommendation: Change verify_api_key to accept session: Session = Depends(get_session), matching get_current_user, or wrap all local database work in an explicit with Session(engine) block that stays alive until the function returns.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Existing auth-adjacent tests exercise successful JWT/API-token paths but do not assert session closure, connection pool behavior, or cleanup on exception paths.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a dependency-level test that overrides get_session with a tracking generator and verifies verify_api_key closes/finishes the session exactly once on success and failure.
